- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction, reducing forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–4% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates the mean reversion phase after a strong rally; if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral, add a 1–3% downward bias for 5–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to over-predict early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; reduce forecast by 2–5% for first 5 days if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment for the 3–5 day window following sentiment shifts.
